mainTopic: Where הבדלה is said, balsam sap as fruit, the 'virgin of blood', and when a pregnancy counts as known
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation of why רבי אלעזר rules like רבי אליעזר that הבדלה is said in הודאה. רבי אליעזר could not have been quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, who was much younger, so the answer is that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל agreed with him. A ברייתא about the prayers of יום הכפורים seems to show otherwise. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that there רבי חנינא בן גמליאל was only reporting his forefathers' view. Next, the גמרא returns to whether רבי אליעזר is the תנא who treats balsam sap as fruit, and it shows that even the רבנן may agree in some cases. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's בתולה, which here means a woman who never saw menstrual blood. It asks why רב כהנא's list of three kinds of בתולה leaves this one out, and several אמוראים give reasons. After that, the גמרא sets three months as the time a pregnancy becomes known. It rules that a pregnant woman who miscarries air keeps her pregnant status. The amud ends with a second ברייתא that seems to contradict that ruling, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר was much older
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier suggestion. רבי אליעזר could not have been quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, because he was much older than him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't he (רבי אליעזר) much older than him (רבי חנינא בן גמליאל)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason just given for why רבי אלעזר follows רבי אליעזר. An older sage would not be quoting a much younger one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous suggestion linked רבי אליעזר's ruling to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, as if רבי אליעזר were quoting him. The problem is about time. רבי אליעזר was from an earlier, older generation, so it makes no sense for him to rely on a younger sage. This knocks out the suggested reason, and the גמרא will need a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: Older, senior in age
Than him
Very much, a lot

phrases.english: But he is much older than him!
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אליעזר, and "him" is רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קַשִּׁישׁ מִינֵּיהּ טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the earlier suggested reason, from before this section, for why רבי אלעזר rules like רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי אליעזר was quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An older sage does not quote a much younger sage, so the suggestion doesn't fit the generations.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל agrees with him
steps.stepSummary: The new reason: רבי אלעזר rules like רבי אליעזר because רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds the same view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because רבי חנינא בן גמליאל stands with his (רבי אליעזר's) opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation. רבי אליעזר wasn't quoting anyone; rather, רבי חנינא בן גמליאל happens to agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying רבי אליעזר learned it from רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, the גמרא says the younger sage held like the older one. Since another sage supports רבי אליעזר's view, רבי אלעזר felt confident ruling like him. The order is reversed: the younger sage follows the older one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new answer after the old one fell
Stands in his approach, meaning he agrees with his opinion

phrases.english: Rather, it is because he stands
Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel, with his opinion.
phrases.notes: "His opinion" means רבי אליעזר's opinion about where הבדלה is said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָאֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּשִׁיטְתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 1 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the relationship: agreement, not quotation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר was quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל agrees with רבי אליעזר, and that support is why רבי אלעזר rules like him.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי חנינא disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי חנינא בן גמליאל really agrees. A ברייתא about the יום הכפורים prayers has him say הבדלה goes in חונן הדעת, not in הודאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really stand with him? But a ברייתא teaches this. On the night of יום הכפורים, one prays seven blessings and confesses. At שחרית, one prays seven and confesses. At מוסף, one prays seven and confesses. At מנחה, one prays seven and confesses. At נעילה, one prays seven and confesses. At ערבית after the fast, one prays seven blessings, a shortened form of the eighteen. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says in the name of his forefathers: one prays the full eighteen, because he must say הבדלה in חונן הדעת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 2. It brings a ברייתא where רבי חנינא בן גמליאל puts הבדלה in a different blessing than רבי אליעזר does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that הבדלה is said in הודאה, one of the last three blessings. That blessing is also part of the shortened seven-blessing prayer. In the ברייתא, רבי חנינא בן גמליאל insists on the full eighteen after יום הכפורים, so that הבדלה can be said in חונן הדעת, which is one of the middle blessings. So he clearly does not hold like רבי אליעזר, and the support claimed in step 2 seems to be gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Confesses sins (וידוי)
The closing prayer at the end of יום הכפורים
A shortened version of the eighteen weekday blessings
The declaration separating holy time from weekday time
The fourth blessing of the weekday עמידה, asking for knowledge

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the list of prayers. The whole ברייתא is brought only for its last line: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל puts הבדלה in חונן הדעת, which clashes with רבי אליעזר's view that it goes in הודאה.

phrases.english: And does he really stand with him? But it is taught:
On the night of Yom Kippur —
one prays seven blessings and confesses;
at the morning prayer — one prays seven and confesses;
at the additional prayer — one prays seven and confesses;
at the afternoon prayer — one prays seven and confesses;
at Ne'ilah — one prays seven and confesses;
at the evening prayer — one prays seven
phrases.notes: This is the evening prayer after the fast ends, which is a regular weekday night.

phrases.english: a shortened form of the eighteen.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִשּׁוּם אֲבוֹתָיו אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says in the name of his forefathers:
one prays the full eighteen,
because he must say havdalah
in "Who graciously grants knowledge."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי קָאֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל agrees with רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל places הבדלה in חונן הדעת, while רבי אליעזר places it in הודאה, so they disagree.

steps.title: He was only quoting his forefathers
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל was reporting his forefathers' view, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He said it in the name of his forefathers, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 3. The ruling in the ברייתא was a report of his forefathers' view, not his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא itself says "in the name of his forefathers." רב נחמן בר יצחק uses that wording to separate the report from what רבי חנינא בן גמליאל personally held. His own view can still match רבי אליעזר, so the answer of step 2 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his forefathers
He himself
He does not hold that way

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר follows רבי אליעזר about saying הבדלה in הודאה because רבי חנינא בן גמליאל agrees with him. The ברייתא that seems to say otherwise is only רבי חנינא בן גמליאל reporting his forefathers' view.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
He said it in the name of his forefathers,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיהוּ אָמַר מִשּׁוּם אֲבוֹתָיו, וְלֵיהּ לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and saves the answer of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution split: a reported view versus a personal view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's own opinion, which disagrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only quoting his forefathers. His own opinion agrees with רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's proof about balsam sap
steps.stepSummary: Going back to an earlier discussion, רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא. Why doubt that רבי אליעזר holds balsam sap counts as fruit? A משנה shows that רבי אליעזר treats the sap of an ערלה tree as forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: And you, don't you hold that the תנא who taught that balsam sap is fruit is רבי אליעזר? But we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says, one who curdles cheese with the sap of ערלה, the cheese is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier topic. רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא, who had doubted that רבי אליעזר is the one who calls balsam sap "fruit."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי זירא questioned the claim that רבי אליעזר is the תנא who treats balsam sap as fruit. רבי ירמיה points to a משנה in ערלה. There, רבי אליעזר forbids cheese curdled with the sap of an ערלה tree. That shows he considers tree sap to be fruit, since ערלה forbids only the fruit of a young tree.

keyTerms.meaning: Balsam sap
Fruit
One who curdles cheese, using a substance to set the milk
Sap or resin of a tree
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
And you, do you not hold
that the one who taught that balsam sap is fruit
is Rabbi Eliezer?
But we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
phrases.notes: משנה ערלה 1:7

phrases.english: One who curdles cheese with the sap of orlah, it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: The cheese is forbidden because רבי אליעזר treats the tree's sap like its fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרַאּ דְּמַאן תְּנָא קִטְפָא פֵּירָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הבדלה discussion and returns to the earlier debate about balsam sap.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's doubt that רבי אליעזר is the תנא who holds balsam sap is fruit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר forbids cheese curdled with the sap of ערלה, so he must treat tree sap as fruit.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds tree sap has the status of fruit
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה ערלה 1:7: הַמַּעֲמִיד בִּשְׂרַף עָרְלָה אָסוּר

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree about sap that comes from fruit
steps.stepSummary: Answering רבי ירמיה, the גמרא says the balsam source could even follow the רבנן. They only argue with רבי אליעזר about sap from the tree's wood. They agree that sap from the fruit counts as fruit, as רבי יהושע taught about unripe figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows the רבנן. The רבנן only disagree with רבי אליעזר about sap that comes from the wood of the tree. About sap that comes from the fruit, they agree with him. As we learned: רבי יהושע said, 'I heard clearly that if someone curdles cheese with sap from the leaves or roots, it is permitted. If he uses sap from unripe figs, it is forbidden, because that sap is fruit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי ירמיה's proof from step 5. The balsam source does not have to be רבי אליעזר, because even the רבנן agree that sap from the fruit counts as fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן is narrowed to sap from the wood of the tree. For sap from the fruit, everyone agrees it counts as fruit. The proof is רבי יהושע: sap from leaves and roots is permitted, but sap from unripe figs is forbidden because it is fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue up to this point (and no further)
Sap or resin that oozes out of a plant
The wood or trunk of the tree
One who curdles milk into cheese
Unripe figs

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן say sap is never fruit. In this answer they only disagree about sap from the wood. Sap from the fruit itself counts as fruit for everyone.

phrases.english: You may even say it follows the Rabbis,
the Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi Eliezer
regarding the sap of the tree's wood,
but regarding the sap of the fruit, they agree with him,
as we learned: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
I heard explicitly
that one who curdles cheese with the sap of the leaves
or with the sap of the roots, it is permitted,
but with the sap of unripe figs, it is forbidden,
because it is fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge in step 5. The ערלה משנה does not prove the balsam תנא is רבי אליעזר, because the רבנן could also hold it, so רבי זירא's doubt can stand.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the argument (wood sap vs. fruit sap)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן reject the idea that sap is fruit in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן only argue about sap from the wood. Sap from the fruit counts as fruit for everyone.

steps.title: Another approach: the רבנן agree about a tree that grows no fruit
steps.stepSummary: A second way to explain it: the רבנן argue only about a fruit-bearing tree. For a tree that grows no fruit, its sap is its fruit, as the חכמים say in a משנה about שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say this instead: the רבנן argue with רבי אליעזר about a tree that makes fruit. About a tree that does not make fruit, they agree that its sap is its fruit. As we learned: רבי שמעון says the laws of שביעית do not apply to sap. The חכמים say they do apply to sap, because its sap is its fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to show that the רבנן can agree sap is fruit. This time the dividing line is whether the tree makes fruit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the split is not wood vs. fruit, but a fruit tree vs. a tree with no fruit. A tree with no fruit has nothing else to count as its 'fruit', so its sap fills that role. The proof is the חכמים in the שביעית משנה, who say sap has שביעית status because 'its sap is its fruit'.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (a second, alternative answer)
A tree that does not produce fruit
Its sap is its fruit
The Sabbatical Year and the special holiness of its produce

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר —
phrases.english: when the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer,
it is about a tree that makes fruit,
but about a tree that does not make fruit,
they agree that its sap is its fruit.
As we learned: Rabbi Shimon says:
Sap does not have Sabbatical Year status,
and the Rabbis say: sap does have Sabbatical Year status,
because its sap is its fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different explanation of where the רבנן agree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative distinction (fruit-bearing tree vs. non-fruit-bearing tree)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן never treat sap as fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a tree that makes no fruit, even the רבנן agree its sap is its fruit.

steps.title: The חכמים in that משנה must be the רבנן who argue with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its proof: the חכמים in the שביעית משנה are presumably the same רבנן who argue with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are these חכמים? Aren't they the same רבנן who argue with רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why the שביעית משנה is a proof. It assumes the 'חכמים' there are the רבנן who disagree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the חכמים who say 'its sap is its fruit' are the same people who argue with רבי אליעזר about sap. If so, those רבנן agree in the case of a tree with no fruit. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?
Is it not? (introduces a question that expects 'yes')
The Sages, usually the majority view against a single תנא

phrases.english: Who are the Rabbis?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר?
phrases.english: Are they not the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן חֲכָמִים? לָאו רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה from step 7 proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן who argue with רבי אליעזר agree sap is fruit in a tree that makes no fruit
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים in the משנה about שביעית and sap

steps.title: An elder quotes רבי יוחנן: those חכמים are רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: An elder pushes back on the proof. He quotes רבי יוחנן that the 'חכמים' in the שביעית משנה are really רבי אליעזר, who holds that sap is fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: Who are the חכמים? It is רבי אליעזר, who said its sap is its fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from step 8 is rejected. According to רבי יוחנן, the 'חכמים' in that משנה are not the רבנן but רבי אליעזר himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 'חכמים' are רבי אליעזר, then the משנה shows nothing about what the רבנן think. So there is no proof that the רבנן agree about a tree that makes no fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder (an unnamed older scholar)

steps.confusionAlert: The word חכמים usually means the majority Sages, but here רבי יוחנן says it refers to one person, רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
This is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Who are the Rabbis? It is Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: its sap is its fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 8 by changing who the 'חכמים' are.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the רבנן agree about a tree that makes no fruit
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים in the שביעית משנה are רבי אליעזר, not the רבנן who argue with him.

steps.title: Why would רבי אליעזר talk only about a tree with no fruit?
steps.stepSummary: If the חכמים are רבי אליעזר, why does the משנה focus on a tree that makes no fruit? He holds that sap is fruit even in a fruit tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי אליעזר, why talk specifically about a tree that does not make fruit? Even in a tree that makes fruit, its sap is its fruit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's reading. רבי אליעזר holds sap is fruit in every tree, so why limit the משנה to a tree that makes no fruit?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to speak about a tree that has no fruit, where sap stands in for fruit. That limit makes sense for the רבנן, but not for רבי אליעזר, who says sap is always fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: If
Why specifically this case? (why limit it to this)

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Eliezer,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִירְיָא אִילָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה פְּרִי?
phrases.english: why specifically a tree that does not make fruit?
Even a tree that makes fruit,
its sap is its fruit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מַאי אִירְיָא אִילָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה פְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's claim from step 9 that the חכמים are רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading that the חכמים in the שביעית משנה are רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר holds sap is fruit in all trees, so limiting the ruling to a tree with no fruit does not fit him.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר argued on the רבנן's own terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר was arguing according to the רבנן's view: 'I say even a fruit tree's sap is fruit, but you should at least agree about a tree with no fruit.' The רבנן answered: there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was speaking to them according to the רבנן's own words: 'In my view, even a tree that makes fruit, its sap is its fruit. In your view, at least agree with me about a tree that does not make fruit, that its sap is its fruit.' And the רבנן said to him: 'There is no difference.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10. רבי אליעזר mentioned a tree with no fruit only to make the smallest claim the רבנן might accept, and the רבנן still said no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's own view did not change: sap is fruit in every tree. He offered the 'no-fruit tree' case as a minimum the רבנן should accept even by their own logic. The רבנן answered 'לא שנא': sap is not fruit in either kind of tree, so the proof that they agree falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their words (arguing from the other side's view)
According to me
According to you (plural)
At least
There is no difference

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the 'חכמים' who say 'its sap is its fruit' are רבי אליעזר. He mentioned a tree with no fruit only as an argument from the רבנן's own view, and the רבנן rejected it: for them sap is not fruit, whether or not the tree makes fruit.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of arguing 'לדבריהם' (on the other side's terms) appears often in the גמרא. A תנא may give a smaller case not because he limits his own view, but to push the other side.

phrases.english: He was speaking to them according to the words of the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי, אֲפִילּוּ אִילָן הָעוֹשֶׂה פֵּירוֹת נָמֵי —
phrases.english: According to me, even a tree that makes fruit too,
its sap is its fruit.
According to you, at least agree with me
about a tree that does not make fruit,
that its sap is its fruit.
And the Rabbis said to him: There is no difference.
phrases.notes: The רבנן mean that sap is not fruit in either kind of tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 and backs up רבי יוחנן's reading from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Arguing on the other side's terms (לדבריהם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning a tree with no fruit means רבי אליעזר limits his own view to that case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר holds sap is always fruit. He gave the no-fruit tree only as a minimum for the רבנן, and they rejected even that.

steps.title: A virgin of blood, not a virgin of the hymen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's definition of בתולה. A ברייתא then explains that even a married woman, or one who gave birth, is still called a בתולה here, as long as she never saw menstrual blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Who is a 'virgin'? Any woman who has never seen menstrual blood. The רבנן taught: If she married and bled because of the marriage, or gave birth and bled because of the birth, I still call her a 'virgin.' The 'virgin' the חכמים meant is a virgin of blood, not a virgin of the hymen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה: who counts as a בתולה. It brings a ברייתא showing that the word means something special here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally בתולה means a woman who never had relations. Here it means a woman who never had a period. So bleeding from marriage or from childbirth does not change her status, because neither of those is menstrual blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally a 'virgin.' Here it means a woman who has never seen menstrual blood.
A 'virgin of blood': a woman who never had a period.
A 'virgin of the hymen': a woman who never had relations.
Because of marriage, meaning bleeding from the first relations.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read בתולה here in its usual sense. In this משנה a married woman who has given birth can still be a בתולה, as long as she never had a period.

phrases.english: Who is a virgin?
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which listed the בתולה among women who do not become טמאה retroactively.

phrases.english: Any woman who has not seen, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
If she married and saw blood because of the marriage,
or gave birth and saw blood because of the birth,
I still call her a "virgin,"
because the "virgin" that they spoke of
is a virgin of blood,
and not a virgin of the hymen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזוֹ הִיא בְּתוּלָה? כֹּל שֶׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה, separate from the sap and fruit discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For נדה, a בתולה is a woman who never saw menstrual blood. Bleeding from marriage or childbirth does not remove that status.

steps.title: רב כהנא's list of three kinds of virgins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of a 'virgin of blood.' It quotes רב כהנא's teaching that there are only three kinds of בתולה, beginning with a human בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? רב כהנא said a ברייתא taught: There are three kinds of virgins: a virgin person, virgin ground, and a virgin sycamore. A virgin person is a woman who has never had relations. This matters for marrying a כהן גדול, or for her כתובה of two hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge with 'אִינִי?' ('Is that so?'). It begins quoting a list of three kinds of בתולה that does not mention a 'virgin of blood.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list defines a human בתולה only by relations, not by menstrual blood. This is the start of the attack. The point will become clear at the end of the quote, in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?' This word opens a challenge.
The practical difference this makes.
The High Priest, who may only marry a בתולה.
A כתובה of two hundred זוז, the amount for a בתולה.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Kahana say:
It was taught: There are three kinds of virgins:

phrases.aramaic: בְּתוּלַת אָדָם, בְּתוּלַת קַרְקַע, בְּתוּלַת שִׁקְמָה.
phrases.english: a virgin person, virgin ground, and a virgin sycamore.
A virgin person:
as long as she has not had relations.
The difference it makes is for a High Priest,
or else, for her marriage contract of two hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's category of a 'virgin of blood.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that there is a 'בתולת דמים' category.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching that lists every kind of בתולה does not include a 'virgin of blood.'

steps.title: Virgin ground and virgin sycamore
steps.stepSummary: The rest of רב כהנא's list: virgin ground is land never worked, and a virgin sycamore is one never cut. Each has practical differences, and the sycamore case is supported by a משנה in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Virgin ground is land that has never been worked. This matters for the 'rough valley' of the עגלה ערופה, or for buying and selling. A virgin sycamore is one that has never been cut down. This matters for buying and selling, or for cutting it in שביעית, as the משנה says: One may not cut a virgin sycamore in שביעית, because that is farm work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רב כהנא's list of three kinds of בתולה. This sets up the punchline of the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of בתולה has its own practical difference. The quote from the שביעית משנה shows that 'virgin sycamore' is a real legal term. Still, nowhere does the list mention a 'virgin of blood.'

keyTerms.meaning: The rough, unworked valley where the עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה is brought.
Buying and selling. It matters what someone meant when he agreed to buy 'virgin' land or trees.
A sycamore tree.
The seventh year, when farm work is forbidden.
Farm work, which is forbidden in שביעית.

phrases.english: Virgin ground:
as long as it has not been worked.
The difference it makes is for the rough valley,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:4. The עגלה ערופה is brought to land that was never worked.

phrases.english: or else, for buying and selling.
A virgin sycamore:
as long as it has not been cut down.
The difference it makes is for buying and selling,
or else, for cutting it down in the seventh year,
as we learned:
One may not cut down a virgin sycamore in the seventh year
because it is work.
phrases.notes: Cutting it down helps the tree grow back stronger, so it counts as farming.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתוּלַת קַרְקַע — כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֶבְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting רב כהנא's list, which step 13 began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Virgin ground is land never worked. A virgin sycamore is one never cut down, and cutting it in שביעית is forbidden as work.

steps.title: Why isn't the virgin of blood on the list?
steps.stepSummary: The punchline of the challenge: if a 'virgin of blood' is a real category, רב כהנא's list should have taught it as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If what the ברייתא said is true, the list should also have taught this kind of virgin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states its challenge outright. The list says 'three' and leaves out the 'virgin of blood.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a teaching gives a number like 'three,' it suggests the list is complete. So leaving out the 'בתולת דמים' suggests no such category exists. That would contradict the ברייתא in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if it is so.' It is used to push a claim to its consequence.
'Let it teach this one too.' This points out that something is missing from a list.

steps.whatToRemember: The question: the ברייתא says there is a 'בתולת דמים,' but רב כהנא's list of exactly three kinds of בתולה does not include it.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if a 'virgin of blood' really is a category.

phrases.english: let it also teach this one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, לִיתְנֵי נָמֵי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the full quoted list and turns it against step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The list gives a number, which suggests it is complete. Since the 'virgin of blood' is missing, the category seems not to exist.

steps.title: First answer: the list only includes names that need no extra word
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רב כהנא lists only things called 'בתולה' with no added word. A 'virgin of blood' always needs the added word 'of blood', so it is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The list only teaches things that have no added name. Things that do have an added name are not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question from Step 15. It explains why רב כהנא did not list a 'virgin of blood'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A virgin woman, virgin ground and a virgin sycamore can each be called just 'בתולה' and everyone understands. A woman who never saw blood can only be called a בתולה with the extra words 'of blood'. רב כהנא's list only counts the plain uses of the word.

keyTerms.meaning: An added name, meaning an extra word attached to describe something
When he teaches, meaning what the list includes
A thing, an item

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָתָנֵי מִידֵּי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ שֵׁם לְוַוי,
phrases.english: When he teaches, it is an item that has no added name,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב כהנא, whose list of three בתולות we just saw.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִידֵּי דְּאִית לֵיהּ שֵׁם לְוַוי — לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: but an item that has an added name, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי מִידֵּי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ שֵׁם לְוַוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what kind of item the list covers (naming rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list should include every use of 'בתולה', including a virgin of blood
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only covers things called 'בתולה' with no extra word

steps.title: Second answer: the list only includes things that depend on an action
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי says the list includes only a 'virginity' that ends through an outside action. Menstrual blood starts on its own, so it is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת the son of רב אידי said: The list only teaches things that depend on an action. Things that do not depend on an action are not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reason why the 'virgin of blood' is not in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman stops being a בתולה through relations. Ground stops being virgin when it is worked, and a sycamore when it is cut. A woman starts seeing blood by herself, with no action done to her, so she does not fit the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Depends on an action that someone does

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said:
When he teaches, it is an item that depends on an action,

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּלָא תְּלֵי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה — לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: an item that does not depend on an action, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי מִידֵּי דִּתְלֵי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what kind of item the list covers (action rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any kind of 'virginity' belongs in the list
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a 'virginity' that ends through an outside action is listed

steps.title: Third answer: the list only includes things that never go back
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בריה דרב איקא says the list includes only things that never return to their first state. A woman's flow stops in old age, so she 'returns', and that case is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא the son of רב איקא said: The list only teaches things that do not go back to their original state. Things that go back are not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא offers another rule to explain why the 'virgin of blood' is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a woman, ground or sycamore loses its 'virginity', it never gets it back. A woman's menstrual blood can stop later in life, so she goes back to having no blood. Since that state can return, it is not counted.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back to its original, natural state

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina, son of Rav Ika, said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָתָנֵי מִידֵּי דְּלָא הָדַר לִבְרִיָּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: When he teaches, it is an item that does not go back to its original state,
an item that goes back to its original state, he does not teach.
phrases.notes: He means a woman's bleeding, which can stop when she gets older.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי מִידֵּי דְּלָא הָדַר לִבְרִיָּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what kind of item the list covers (permanence rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any kind of 'virginity' belongs in the list
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a loss of 'virginity' that is permanent is listed

steps.title: Fourth answer: the list only includes things a buyer cares about
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the list includes only things a buyer cares about. He assumes a man marrying a woman does not care whether she has seen blood, so that case is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The list only teaches things a buyer is particular about. Things a buyer is not particular about are not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a fourth reason, based on what matters to a buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone buying land or a sycamore cares whether it is 'virgin', and a husband cares whether his bride is a בתולה. רבינא assumes nobody cares whether a woman has started seeing blood. The next step will attack that assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: Is particular, cares about it
A buyer

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָתָנֵי מִידֵּי דְּקָפֵיד עֲלֵיהּ זָבוֹנָא,
phrases.english: When he teaches, it is an item that a buyer is particular about,

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּלָא קָפֵיד עֲלֵיהּ זָבוֹנָא לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: an item that a buyer is not particular about, he does not teach.
phrases.notes: For a woman, the 'buyer' is the man who wants to marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי מִידֵּי דְּקָפֵיד עֲלֵיהּ זָבוֹנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what kind of item the list covers (buyer's concern)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any kind of 'virginity' belongs in the list
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a 'virginity' a buyer cares about is listed

steps.title: Challenge: a husband does care about a woman's blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether buyers really do not care. Two ברייתות say blood is good for a woman and a sign she will have many children, so a husband would care.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they are not particular? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי חייא says: Just as leaven is good for dough, so blood is good for a woman. And another ברייתא teaches in the name of רבי מאיר: Any woman whose blood is plentiful has many children!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא's answer. It argues that a husband would care whether a woman sees blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's answer assumed nobody cares whether a woman has blood. רבי חייא compares blood to leaven that makes dough rise, and רבי מאיר links much blood to many children. So blood does matter to a husband, and רבינא's reason seems to fall.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven, sourdough starter that makes dough rise
Dough
Many, plentiful

phrases.english: And they are not particular?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Ḥiyya says:
Just as leaven is good for dough,
so blood is good for a woman.
And it is taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁדָּמֶיהָ מְרוּבִּין — בָּנֶיהָ מְרוּבִּין!
phrases.english: Any woman whose blood is plentiful, her children are plentiful!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא קָפְדִי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבינא's answer in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that a buyer does not care about a woman's blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות show blood is a good sign for a woman and her children, so a husband would care

steps.title: Reworded answer: the list includes things buyers are eager for
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes רבינא's rule by one letter, from קפיד (particular) to קפיץ (eager). Buyers run after a virgin woman, field or sycamore, but nobody runs after a woman who has no blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the list only teaches things a buyer jumps to get. Things a buyer does not jump to get are not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבינא's answer so that it fits the ברייתות it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is no longer that buyers do not care. Now the point is what buyers are eager for. A man runs to marry a בתולה, but nobody runs to marry a woman with no blood, since blood is a good sign. A 'virgin of blood' is not something people want, so it is not on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Jumps at, is eager to get

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up קָפֵיד (particular, cares about) from Step 19 with קָפֵיץ (jumps at, is eager for) here. The words differ by one letter, but the new answer is that buyers are not eager for a woman without blood.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four rules for why רב כהנא's list leaves out the 'virgin of blood': it needs an extra word, it does not depend on an action, it can go back to its first state, and buyers are not eager for it. That last rule replaces רבינא's first version, 'buyers do not care'.

phrases.english: Rather, when he teaches —
it is an item that a buyer jumps at,

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּלָא קָפֵיץ עֲלֵיהּ זָבוֹנָא — לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: an item that a buyer does not jump at, he does not teach.
phrases.notes: Since blood is a good sign, nobody is eager for a woman who has none.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי קָתָנֵי מִידֵּי דְּקָפֵיץ עֲלֵיהּ זָבוֹנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 by rewording רבינא's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the rule (קפיד becomes קפיץ)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Buyers do not care about a woman's blood
steps.terutzMaskana: Buyers care, but they are not eager for a woman without blood, so it is not listed

steps.title: How to recognize virgin ground
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines virgin ground: it comes up in hard clumps and its dirt is not loose. A pottery shard shows it was worked before, while hard rock shows it is virgin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: What is 'virgin ground'? Any ground that comes up in hard clumps and whose dirt is not loose. If a pottery shard is found in it, it is known that it was worked. If hard rock is found, it is virgin ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives signs for telling whether ground is virgin, the second item in רב כהנא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ground that was never plowed is hard and comes up in solid clumps, not loose dirt. A piece of pottery means people were there and worked the land, so it is not virgin. Solid rock in the ground is a sign that it was never touched.

keyTerms.meaning: Hard clumps of earth
Loose, soft (dirt)
A shard of pottery
Hard rock
Was worked (plowed or farmed)

phrases.english: The Sages taught: What is 'virgin ground'?
Any ground that brings up hard clumps,
and whose dirt is not loose.
If a pottery shard is found in it, it is known that it was worked.
If hard rock is found, this is 'virgin ground'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזוֹהִי בְּתוּלַת קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why the list is limited to defining one of its items (virgin ground)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Virgin ground comes up in hard clumps and is not loose. A pottery shard shows it was worked, and hard rock shows it is virgin.

steps.title: When is a pregnancy considered known?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about a מעוברת and asks how long it takes until her pregnancy is recognizable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a pregnant woman counts from when her fetus is known. How long until a fetus is known?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and asks a clarifying question about it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a pregnant woman is impure only from the moment she sees blood, not backward in time. That leniency starts once her pregnancy is known, so the גמרא needs to know exactly when that is.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant woman
From when her fetus becomes known
The point when the fetus can be recognized

phrases.english: A pregnant woman: from when her fetus is known.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה: a pregnant woman is impure only from the moment she sees blood, once her pregnancy is known.

phrases.english: And how long until the fetus is recognizable?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה הַכָּרַת הָעוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of virgin ground and returns to the משנה's next case, the pregnant woman.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much time must pass before a pregnancy counts as known.

steps.title: Three months, hinted at in the story of תמר
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס, quoting רבי מאיר, says three months, and brings a hint from the פסוק about תמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: סומכוס said in the name of רבי מאיר: three months. There is no real proof, but there is a hint: 'And it was about three months later...'
steps.whatsHappening: סומכוס answers the question: a pregnancy is known after three months. He supports it with a פסוק but calls it only a hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תמר story, people noticed she was pregnant about three months in. רבי מאיר uses that as a hint that a pregnancy shows after three months, but he says clearly that it is not a full proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint or reminder for the idea, weaker than a proof
A real proof for the idea
Three months

phrases.english: Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Three months.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint for the matter,
as it says: 'And it was about three months later, etc.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:24. That is when יהודה was told that תמר was pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹמְכוֹס אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A pregnancy is considered known after three months.

steps.title: Why call a clear פסוק only a hint?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר calls the פסוק only a hint when it seems to be a strong proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only a hint? A פסוק is written there, and that is a big proof!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's modest wording. The פסוק says three months openly, so why not call it a proof?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not against the ruling of three months. It is against calling the source a זכר לדבר when it looks like a direct proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק is written
A strong proof

phrases.english: Only a hint for the matter?
A פסוק is written, and it is a strong proof!

steps.triggerLanguage: זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר? קְרָא כְּתִיב, וּרְאָיָה גְּדוֹלָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the answer in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's calling the תמר פסוק only a זכר לדבר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק openly says three months, so it should count as a real proof.

steps.title: Pregnancies differ in length
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק cannot fully prove the rule, because some women give birth after nine months and some after seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because some women give birth at nine months and some give birth at seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק is only a hint. Pregnancies are not all the same length, so one story cannot set the rule for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three months is one third of a nine-month pregnancy. If תמר's pregnancy was nine months long, a seven-month pregnancy might show at a third of its term, which is earlier. So the פסוק does not prove that three months is the right measure for every woman, and רבי מאיר sets three months for all cases while calling the פסוק only a hint.

keyTerms.meaning: There is, there are
She gives birth after nine months
She gives birth after seven months

steps.whatToRemember: A pregnancy counts as known after three months. The תמר פסוק is only a hint for this, because pregnancies differ in length.

phrases.english: Because there is a woman who gives birth at nine months,
and there is a woman who gives birth at seven.
phrases.notes: So what was true for תמר might not be true for every woman, and the פסוק cannot be a full proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא דְּיָלְדָה לְתִשְׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the strength of the proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק directly proves three months for every woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק may fit only one length of pregnancy, so it is only a hint.

steps.title: A miscarriage of air does not cancel pregnant status
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a woman presumed pregnant who saw blood and then miscarried air or a non-viable fetus keeps her pregnant status, so she is impure only from when she saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who was presumed pregnant, saw blood, and then miscarried air or anything not viable keeps her status, and she is impure only from the moment she saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a pregnancy that did not end with a real baby. Even so, the woman is treated as a מעוברת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that if no living child came out, she was never really pregnant and loses the leniency of דיה שעתה. The ברייתא says no: she keeps her pregnant status, so the blood she saw makes her impure only from then on and not backward in time.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumed to be pregnant
She miscarried
Viable, able to live
Her time is enough: she is impure only from when she sees, not backward

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If a woman was presumed pregnant,
and she saw blood,
and afterward she miscarried air

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁל קְיָימָא —
phrases.english: or anything that is not viable,
she keeps her status,
phrases.notes: Meaning she still counts as a pregnant woman.

phrases.english: and her time is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיְתָה בְּחֶזְקַת מְעוּבֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related case about the pregnant woman's status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman presumed pregnant keeps her status even if she miscarries air or a non-viable fetus, so דיה שעתה still applies to her.

steps.title: A hint from ישעיהו: 'we gave birth to wind'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a hint from a פסוק showing that someone who 'gives birth to wind' is still called pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no proof for this, there is a hint: 'We were pregnant, we were in pain, as if we gave birth to wind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא supports its ruling with a פסוק, but again calls it only a hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word 'pregnant' even though what came out was only wind. That fits the ruling that a pregnancy ending in air was still a real pregnancy.

keyTerms.meaning: We were pregnant, we were in pain
We gave birth to wind

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint for the matter,
as it says: 'We were pregnant, we were in pain, as if we gave birth to wind.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 26:18.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and gives a hint for its ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That a pregnancy ending in air or a non-viable miscarriage still counts as a pregnancy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 26:18, which calls those who 'gave birth to wind' pregnant.

steps.title: Again: why only a hint?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא calls the ישעיהו פסוק a hint, since it looks like a strong proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is this called a hint? It is a strong proof!
steps.whatsHappening: Just like before, the גמרא challenges the modest label 'hint' for a פסוק that seems clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק openly calls the speakers pregnant even though they produced only wind. That seems to prove the ברייתא's ruling directly.

keyTerms.meaning: What, why
But surely it is

phrases.english: Why is it called a hint for the matter?
It is a strong proof!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר? הֲרֵי רְאָיָה גְּדוֹלָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 25, now aimed at the ישעיהו פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: Calling the ישעיהו פסוק only a זכר לדבר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק directly links 'pregnant' with 'giving birth to wind', so it should count as a proof.

steps.title: The פסוק speaks about men
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is said about men, who cannot really give birth, so it is a picture and can only be a hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: When this פסוק was written, it was written about men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not about real pregnancy at all. It is a picture spoken by men, so it cannot give a full proof about women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Men do not become pregnant, so the פסוק's 'pregnancy' is only a figure of speech. A halachic rule about women cannot be fully proven from words used as a picture, so it stays a זכר לדבר.

keyTerms.meaning: This פסוק
It is written about males

steps.whatToRemember: A woman presumed pregnant keeps that status even if she miscarries air. Both פסוקים in this section are only hints: the first because pregnancies vary in length, the second because it speaks about men.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא rejects the ruling here. It only explains why the פסוק is called a hint. The ruling of the ברייתא stays in place.

phrases.english: When this פסוק was written,
it was written about males.
phrases.notes: Men can't really be pregnant, so the words are only a picture, not a real case to learn from.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי כְּתִיב הַאי קְרָא בִּזְכָרִים כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the strength of the proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ישעיהו פסוק directly proves the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks about men as a picture, so it is only a hint.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says miscarrying wind is not a real birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts the earlier ברייתא with another one. There, a woman who labored for two days and miscarried wind or a non-viable fetus on the third day is called a woman who gives birth as a זבה. The גמרא starts to explain why this clashes with the idea that such a miscarriage is a proper birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction: If a woman had labor pains for two days, and on the third day she miscarried wind or anything that is not viable, she is considered one who gives birth as a זבה. And if you say that this is a proper birth, [this is a problem...]
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that seems to contradict the one from step 27. It begins to spell out the problem, and the sentence continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27, miscarrying wind did not take away the woman's pregnant status, so it seemed to count as a real pregnancy. Here, a woman who miscarried wind after two days of labor is still treated as a זבה. That suggests the miscarriage does not count as a real birth. The גמרא starts to say: if it were a proper birth, this ruling would not make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: "And raise a contradiction": the גמרא sets one source against another source that seems to say the opposite
She had a hard labor, meaning labor pains
Not viable, something that could not live
A woman who gives birth while she has the status of a זבה
A proper, full-fledged birth

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In step 27 the woman was already presumed pregnant, and the question was when her impurity starts. Here the question is whether the blood she saw during labor counts as זוב. Both cases depend on one issue: does miscarrying wind count as a real birth?

phrases.english: And raise a contradiction: if she had labor pains for two days,
phrases.notes: Literally "she had difficulty": she had labor pains, and during them she saw blood.

phrases.english: and on the third day she miscarried wind

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁל קְיָימָא —
phrases.english: or anything that is not viable,
she is a woman who gives birth as a זבה.
And if you say it is a proper birth,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling why the ישעיהו פסוק is only a hint, the גמרא challenges the ruling of the ברייתא from step 27 with a second ברייתא that seems to rule the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 27 that miscarrying wind or a non-viable fetus still counts as a real pregnancy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second ברייתא treats the woman as a זבה even though she miscarried wind after labor. This implies the miscarriage is not a proper birth. That clashes with treating it as a real pregnancy, and the גמרא begins to state this clash with "if you say it is a proper birth."
